To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

agency theory is more likely to prevail if the owner is absent and if the CFO is young and has a short-term management contract, whereas stewardship theory is more likely if the owner is present and if the CFO has a long-term management contract, is older and is wealthy.

the CFOs of privately held firms are more likely to act in a stewardship manner when they report to owner-managers, when the owner-manager's goals are long-term and when the owner-manager is involved in management.

agency attitudes of CFOs are positively influenced by the existence of short-term management appointments and negatively by the existence of owners in management, and stewardship attitudes are positively influenced by CFO maturity and negatively by the perceived level of owner influence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the agency or stewardship perspective is more appropriate to describe the role of salaried managers in private companies.
the role of the stewardship and agency theory in private companies.
the role of the salaried CFO in private companies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CFOs in our study are not as much in favor of stewardship behavior as they are in favor of an agency attitude.
the CFO's attitude is influenced by the owner's attitude.
the stewardship and agency theory are not competing theories, but rather complementary theories, which together provide a better understanding of the CFO's role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
agency and stewardship attitudes are not only influenced by individual and organizational factors but also by factors that are related to the principal-agent relationship.
the CFO's stewardship attitude is positively influenced by long-term management appointments, the presence of owner–managing directors, and the maturity in terms of wealth and age of the CFO.
agency and stewardship are not mutually exclusive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
agency and stewardship attitudes are not only a matter of the individual manager's character and values.
the stewardship and agency behavior of salaried managers is influenced by the actions of owners.
the stewardship and agency behavior of salaried managers is influenced by the way owners exercise their power.
